clue.text: Descending in lordly fashion, sportsman's welcomed into the hunt

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsman who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University
a novice fox-hunter is blooded, smeared with the blood of the first kill, as an initiation

explanation.surface: An aristocratic sportsman is formally welcomed into the local hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has' and joins the two pieces. A Blue is an Oxbridge sporting honour; blooding is the old fox-hunting initiation rite.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristocrats are said to have blue blood, so descent from noble lineage is the sense.

clue.text: Stinking fish held up

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the word fish's synonym is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dab is a small flatfish

explanation.surface: A rotten fish is being held aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone off and smelly is described as bad, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Circulate nameless fruitcake

indicators.note: nameless says N, the abbreviation for name, is removed from the synonym

parts.note: a fruitcake is slang for a crazy person, a nutter

explanation.surface: An instruction to pass around a fruitcake whose maker is unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter forged money or documents is to put them into circulation, a legal sense.

clue.text: French goodies?

parts.note: the French word for good is bon, so goodies in French would be that word doubled and pluralised; really they are sweets

explanation.surface: A question about French treats.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweets are goodies, and their name doubles the French word for good.

clue.text: Gapes more fixedly when abroad on flights, say

parts.note: someone abroad is out of the country

indicators.note: say signals that the synonym for flights is only to sound like the letters entered

parts.note: flights of steps are stairs

explanation.surface: Someone stares hard at things while travelling abroad on aeroplanes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flights' suggests air travel, matching 'abroad', but it means flights of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstare someone is to stare at them longer and harder than they can manage.

clue.text: Trick with three kings not hard for Greek

parts.note: to do someone is to trick or swindle them

indicators.note: not says the letters of the word hard are removed from the name

parts.note: England has had three kings named Richard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A card trick played with three kings is easy, for a Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three kings' looks like a card hand, but it is a name borne by three English kings; 'not hard' strips HARD from it, leaving RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the ancient Greek dialects and architectural orders, so it is Greek in kind.

clue.text: Extremely dense hedge gives protection

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extremities, the first and last letters, of dense

parts.note: a hedge serves as a fence round a field

explanation.surface: A thick hedge keeps a garden safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A defence is a means of protection against attack.

clue.text: Backing for carpet is the normal amount

indicators.note: backing says the word for carpet is read in reverse

parts.note: to carpet someone is to reprimand them, to rap them

explanation.surface: Underlay for a carpet is the usual quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the standard or normal level, as in feeling below par.

clue.text: Bedding friendly fool? I say!

indicators.note: I say signals that the words pally and ass are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: friendly is pally and a fool is an ass

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a matey idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A palliasse is a straw-filled mattress, a form of bedding.

clue.text: The board is made up of such ordinary people

definitions.text: The board is made up of such

explanation.surface: Ordinary people make up the board of a company.
explanation.walkthrough: A chessboard is made up of ranks (rows) and files (columns); 'the board' suggests a company's directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank and file are the common members of an organisation as against its leaders; ranks and files form a chessboard.

clue.text: One sets off, having turned round to hold on

indicators.note: to hold says the reversed word takes the next piece inside it
round says the word for turned is read backwards

parts.note: turned means rotated
taken as written

explanation.surface: A person sets off, having turned back to hang on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' looks like the verb of the surface, but it gives ROTATED; 'round' turns that into DETATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A detonator is the device that sets off an explosive charge.

clue.text: Look into where Hereward sheltered criminal

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Hereward the Wake held out against the Normans in the Fens of eastern England
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Investigate where the outlaw Hereward hid a wanted man.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereward the Wake was an English rebel based in the Fens, marshland of eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is someone who has committed a serious crime.

clue.text: A number at: meeting switch off

explanation.surface: A note jotted at a meeting about switching something off.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnout is the number attending an event; to turn out the light is to switch it off.

clue.text: Leader in the field has scent on jacket

parts.note: the scent an animal leaves is its trail
a blazer is a kind of jacket

explanation.surface: The front-runner in a hunt has picked up a scent on a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailblazer is a pioneer, the first in a field of endeavour.

clue.text: Two containers brought to a wine-shop

parts.note: a can is a container
a tin is another container

explanation.surface: Two crates are delivered to a wine shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantina is a Spanish or Italian bar or wine-shop.

clue.text: Part of Italian designer range

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A selection from an Italian designer's collection.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the great mountain range of South America.

clue.text: Intruded on stud and bride in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means the letters of stud and bride are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone burst in on a groom and bride whose clothes were dishevelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude on someone is to disturb them, a synonym.

clue.text: Again force editor to be silenced

parts.note: re is a prefix meaning again
to press is to force

explanation.surface: A journalist is forced once more to keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Repressed means held down or stifled, so kept silent.

clue.text: With a phone, men ordered remarkable things

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Some men with a telephone placed orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' turns PHONE into PHENO; MEN already sits in place, so only PHONE needs shuffling, and A closes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable occurrences or marvels.

clue.text: Fail to keep order and go down in class

parts.note: to lose something is to fail to keep it
a caste is a social order or class

explanation.surface: A teacher can't control the class and falls in standing.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose caste is to drop in social standing, an idiom from the Hindu caste system.

clue.text: They can't charge this for the house wine!

definitions.text: They can't charge this for the house wine!

parts.words: They can't charge this for the house wine!
parts.note: a restaurant's own wine is not brought in by the customer, so no fee for opening a bottle applies

explanation.surface: A diner's quip about restaurant wine charges.
explanation.definitionFit: Corkage is the fee a restaurant charges for opening wine the customer brings.

clue.text: Old boy and high priest at daggers drawn

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
Eli was the high priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A former pupil and a high priest are bitter enemies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at daggers drawn' reads as hostility, but obeli are the printed dagger marks.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelus is the dagger symbol used in printing, so drawn daggers are its plural.

clue.text: Casual labourer not working at first

indicators.note: at first says this piece comes before the other

parts.note: a machine that is not working is off
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: A temporary labourer who did nothing to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: Offhand means casual or nonchalant in manner.

clue.text: Art gallery's in a series of flaps

parts.note: the Louvre is the great art gallery in Paris
the possessive ending supplies its letter as written

explanation.surface: The gallery's paintings hang among some flapping shutters.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s of the possessive is read as a plain letter, turning the gallery's name into a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Louvres are sets of angled slats in a window or vent, a series of flaps.

clue.text: Moved silently in vestment

explanation.surface: A priest crept about in his robes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stole is the past tense of steal, to move stealthily; a stole is a priest's vestment.

clue.text: Bad team illegally ahead

parts.note: food that has gone bad is off
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A poor team got ahead by breaking the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, a player is offside if illegally ahead of the ball when it is played.
explanation.definitionFit: Being offside means being positioned illegally ahead of play.

clue.text: Is cut off, causing stress

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of is cut are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being cut off causes anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: An ictus is the stress on a syllable in verse, a prosody term.

clue.text: Perhaps crossing some African species

explanation.surface: A crossing point used by animals in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: A zebra crossing is a British pedestrian crossing with black-and-white stripes.
explanation.definitionFit: A zebra crossing is one kind of road crossing; zebras are a group of African equine species.

clue.text: Exaggerated as a result of Edward grabbing the bill

indicators.note: grabbing says the first pieces hold the next one inside

parts.note: over can mean because of, as in a row over money
Ed is short for Edward
a bill becomes an Act once passed by Parliament

explanation.surface: Something was overstated after Edward seized the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To overact is to exaggerate a performance.

clue.text: It's expected in deserts

explanation.surface: Something expected in deserts, perhaps rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something due is expected; one's due is what one deserves, one's deserts.

clue.text: First half of conundrum is clear

indicators.note: first half of asks for the opening half of the word for conundrum

parts.note: a conundrum is a riddle

explanation.surface: Half a puzzle is solved.
explanation.definitionFit: To rid a place of something is to clear it.

clue.text: Ireland's leader working with smile

indicators.note: working means the letters of leader and smile are set to work in a new order

explanation.surface: The Irish leader is busy smiling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emerald Isle is a poetic name for Ireland, after its green landscape.
